title: Microsoft Teams: users can report a security concern in meetings
summary: The default, licensing and reporting workflows are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. The meeting-reporting admin path is not an actionable navigation route: Microsoft names the setting but does not identify the policy or settings page needed to reach it.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Policy or settings page that controls reporting for Teams meetings > Allow users to report meetings is the navigation path to meeting reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center "Allow users to report meetings" navigation ReportMeeting; opened end-user-reporting-teams-meeting and submissions-teams. They name the policy but describe the first page generically, without a selectable navigation label.
claims.fix: Remove the generic navigation string from controls[0].ui and the rendered table; set that side to null. Retain the setting name in the note: 'Microsoft documents Allow users to report meetings in the Teams admin center, but has not published its navigation path.' Keep the documented PowerShell alternative.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -ReportMeeting Enabled|Disabled controls meeting reporting tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Controls whether end users can access the "Report a concern" and "Report as not a concern" options in the meeting experience (including meeting UI and meeting chat).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Global Administrator or Teams Administrator can configure user reporting in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in the Teams admin center, you need to be a member of the **Global Administrator**^\*^ or **Teams Administrator** roles.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify ReportMeeting as the backing setting for the Allow users to report meetings admin toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: "ReportMeeting" "Allow users to report meetings". Read the meeting reporting page, submissions-teams and Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration; both controls are described, but no explicit backing-setting mapping is given.

claims.claim: The dedicated meeting-reporting Learn page remains labelled Preview.
claims.quote: # Report a security concern in Microsoft Teams meetings (Preview)

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the full navigation path to Allow users to report meetings.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center "Allow users to report meetings" navigation ReportMeeting. Opened the dedicated meeting page and submissions-teams; the former says 'open the policy or settings page' without naming that page.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The destination setting is at Defender portal > Settings > Email & collaboration > Teams user reported settings tab > Reported item destinations > Send the reported items to.
claims.quote: go to **Settings** > **Email & collaboration** > **Teams user reported settings** tab.

claims.claim: The printed Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy call sends reported Teams items to Microsoft and the reporting mailbox.
claims.quote:
Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy -Identity DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy `
    -ReportChatMessageEnabled $true `
    -ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled $true `
    -ReportChatMessageAddresses "securityadmin@contoso.com"

claims.claim: Meetings and participant reports follow the same Teams user reported destination settings as other Teams items.
claims.quote: When users report Teams messages or calls or report meetings or meeting participants as malicious or non malicious, the reported items are sent to Microsoft and/or the reporting mailbox as defined by the [Teams user reported settings in Defender for Office 365]

claims.claim: Reported-item destinations are an organization-wide setting.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the report submission policy that you want to modify. The only available policy is named DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy.

claims.claim: The reported-item destination command is run through Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in Teams by using PowerShell, connect to [Exchange Online PowerShell]

claims.claim: Defender monitoring is at Settings > Email & collaboration > Teams user reported settings tab > Microsoft Teams > Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: On the **Teams user reported settings** page, go to the **Microsoft Teams** section for the **Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams** setting.

claims.claim: An automation operation for the Defender monitoring toggle is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams" PowerShell Graph ReportSubmissionPolicy. Read submissions-teams and searched Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy's Teams parameters; they configure destinations, not this monitoring toggle.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Organization Management or Security Administrator can modify the Defender monitoring setting.
claims.quote: To modify the **Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams** setting in the Defender portal, you need to be a member of the **Organization Management** or **Security Administrator** role groups.

claims.claim: Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams is on by default for new tenants.
claims.quote: The **Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams** setting is turned on by default for new tenants; existing tenants need to enable it.

claims.claim: Existing tenants need to enable Defender monitoring.
claims.quote: The **Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams** setting is turned on by default for new tenants; existing tenants need to enable it.

claims.claim: The Defender monitoring setting is meaningful only when Teams reporting is enabled.
claims.quote: The **Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams** setting is meaningful only if Teams message, call, or meeting reporting is turned on in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Defender monitoring must also be enabled for reported items to show correctly on the User reported tab.
claims.quote: it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported items to show up correctly on the **User reported** tab on the **Submissions** page.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Reported meetings can be reviewed at Defender portal > Submissions > User reported tab.
claims.quote: The **User reported** tab of the **Submissions** page at https://security.microsoft.com/reportsubmission?viewid=user:
claims.fix: Use the fuller path 'Actions & submissions > Submissions > User reported tab' and add https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/submissions-admin to sources. Its 'Admin options for user reported messages' section gives Actions & submissions > Submissions; the cited SecOps guide confirms meeting reports on that page.

claims.claim: An API or command for reviewing reported meeting submissions is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting user reported submissions Microsoft Graph API security report review. Read submissions-teams and mdo-support-teams-sec-ops-guide; results describe portal review, not a meeting-submissions API.

claims.claim: The notice makes detailed Defender meeting submissions available to organizations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 1, Plan 2 or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: Organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1, Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR will be able to review detailed reported meeting submissions in the Microsoft Defender portal.

claims.claim: Meeting submission details are also reachable through View submission in the Defender XDR incident.
claims.quote:
SecOps team members can review submitted Teams message, call, meeting, or meeting participant details in the following locations in the Defender portal:

- The **View submission** action in the Defender XDR incident.

claims.claim: Alert policies are at Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Alert policy.
claims.quote: To view and create alert policies, in the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com), under **Email & collaboration** select **Policies & rules** > **Alert policy**.

claims.claim: No supported command for changing the built-in reported-call alert policies is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-ProtectionAlert built-in default alert policies Teams call reported by user. Read alert-policies and the Set-ProtectionAlert search excerpt: 'You can't use this cmdlet to edit default alert policies.' No other supported editing command was found.

claims.claim: Reported meetings and participants generate the same alert policies as reported calls.
claims.quote: Reported meetings and meeting participants generate the same alert policies as reported calls.

claims.claim: Manage Alerts is required to create and edit alert policies.
claims.quote: You have to be assigned the Manage Alerts role to create and edit alert policies.

claims.claim: Built-in alert policies can be turned off and back on.
claims.quote: You can turn off these policies (or back on again), set up a list of recipients to send email notifications to, and set a daily notification limit.

claims.claim: Notification recipients can be configured for built-in alert policies.
claims.quote: You can turn off these policies (or back on again), set up a list of recipients to send email notifications to, and set a daily notification limit.

claims.claim: A daily notification limit can be set for built-in alert policies.
claims.quote: You can turn off these policies (or back on again), set up a list of recipients to send email notifications to, and set a daily notification limit.

claims.claim: Other built-in alert policy settings cannot be edited.
claims.quote: The other settings for these policies can't be edited.

claims.claim: User reports are at Teams admin center > Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports tab > User reported security submissions.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Analytics & reports** > **Protection reports**.
2. On the **View reports** tab, under **Report**, select **User reported security submissions**.
claims.fix: Add the omitted heading: 'Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports tab > Report > User reported security submissions'. The existing note about the documented report categories can remain.

claims.claim: Automation for the Teams admin center User reported security submissions report is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "User reported security submissions" Graph PowerShell API. Read end-user-reported-security-signal; results returned unrelated usage-report commands, not this protection report's API.

claims.claim: The Teams admin report documentation lists Calling, Chats and channels, and User categories.
claims.quote:
Under **Report category**, choose one of the following categories:

    - **Calling**
    - **Chats and channels**
    - **User**

claims.claim: A meetings category in the Teams admin center report is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "User reported security submissions" "meetings" "category". Read end-user-reported-security-signal; its category list contains Calling, Chats and channels, and User, but not Meetings.
